- `env_tree_deciduous`

- `env_tree_conifer`
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picea_abies (Norway spruce 35-55 m)
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinus_sylvestris (Scots pine mature trees about 35 m)
- `env_tree_birch`
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betula_pendula (silver birch 15-25 m, occasionally 31 m)
- `env_tree_palm`
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_dactylifera (height up to about 30 m; crown spans about 6-10 m, fronds 4-6 m)
- `env_bush`
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corylus_avellana (common hazel usually 3-8 m tall)
- `env_grass_clump`
  - General botany reference for tussock grasses (e.g. Wikipedia: Bunchgrass) (clump spread and height)
- `env_rock`
  - Geology general knowledge; glacial erratics (Wikipedia: Glacial erratic) (typical boulder size)
- `env_house_farm`
  - Rural architecture references (e.g. Wikipedia: Farmhouse, Hallenhaus; Fachwerkhaus) (typical footprint and ridge height)
- `env_barn`
  - Rural architecture references (e.g. Wikipedia: Barn) (typical footprint and ridge height)
- `env_house_stone`
  - Rural/village architecture references (e.g. Wikipedia: Vernacular architecture) (typical footprint and ridge height)
- `env_house_mud`
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adobe (adobe bricks e.g. 25x10x36 cm; walls rarely above two storeys)
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mudbrick (construction material only, no dwelling dimensions)
- `env_church`
  - Church architecture references (e.g. Wikipedia: Church (building), Parish church) (typical nave size and tower height)
- `env_bridge_wood`
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timber_bridge (general bridge type only; example Rudolf IV bridge about 4 m wide)
  - US Army FM 5-15 / FM 5-34 timber bridging (not checked for this entry) (none, dimensions are judgement values)
- `env_bridge_stone`
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arch_bridge (general bridge type only, no typical road-bridge dimensions)
- `env_fence_wood`
  - Rural construction practice; typical post-and-rail fence (Wikipedia: Fence) (post spacing and fence height)
- `env_wall_stone`
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_stone (dry-stone wall form; Cornish hedge rule height = base width, top half of base width)
- `env_pole_telegraph`
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utility_pole (UK poles typically 8-10 m long, US about 10 m (about 2 m buried); Morse 1844 posts at least 8 in butt diameter)
- `env_hay_bale`
  - Agricultural history references (e.g. Wikipedia: Haystack) (typical size of a period loose haystack/rick)
- `env_crate`
  - US Army ordnance packing practice (e.g. wooden ammunition box for .50 cal, about 0.4 m scale) (approximate crate size)
- `env_barrel`
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_(container) (200 l steel drum outside diameter about 584 mm, height 876 mm (ANSI MH2))
